items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: I knew Jerome, I knew Jerry Dodgion, Eddie Daniels a little bit. I didn't know them well.

ctx.x: Do you remember the first time you did a session where you sat down and it was an uh oh, maybe because everything was like written out?

Oh yeah. Oh I’ll give you a good one. Oliver Nelson. Right? And I get this call and I go in and it’s a whole sax section you know, it was a big band and me. I forgot what record it was for something, and it was for an introduction, an eight-bar introduction with the sax section in unison with the guitar, playing lines, like bebop, fast bebop lines. And I looked at it and it just all looked like black to me. I couldn’t figure out what it was. And thank God the tape machine broke and somebody said, “Guys, take a 15…

oh, and I’m supposed to play it in unison. So I’ll never forget, I took the music, I went into the bathroom, because I had studied theory so I could solfege in my head and I figured if I could sing it to myself in my head then I could translate it to the guitar. So I went in the stall and I actually was so stressed out that this was the session where they’re going to find out I’m not that good, I threw up in the toilet. I was so nervous. Then I just sat there and kept looking at it and like learned it in my head.…
